text:
aj: Anyone else seeing GPU provisioning failures in us-west2? Several node boots failed with kubelet stuck on mounting ephemeral volumes, logs show device busy on /dev/nvme0n1 :grimacing:
kevin: yep, saw this earlier — batch scheduler reports pods pending because node status NotReady. dmesg shows repeated writeback stall and 'blk_update_request: I/O error' on nvme.
maria: paging infra-oncall, now. I've opened PD: INC12345
infra-oncall: taking it. quick status: 12 nodes affected, mostly gpu-pool-3. Starting root cause triage.
aj: past 2 deploys pushed scrub daemon config change? I noticed scrub interval bumped from 6h -> 1h last night.
kevin: there's a PR that tightened ephemeral-cleaner aggressive GC for disk pressure. Could be causing long writeback bursts.
infra-oncall: grabbing logs, sharing snapshots.
infra-oncall: log excerpt:
```
Apr 03 02:12:11 gnode-173 kernel: nvme0: writeback stall detected, pid=621(kubelet)
Apr 03 02:12:12 gnode-173 kernel: blk_update_request: critical target kernel: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678
Apr 03 02:12:13 gnode-173 kubelet[621]: E0412 02:12:13.123456   621 kubelet_node_status.go:268] failed to update node status: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded
```
kevin: fwiw smartctl reports high media wear but no outright failure; firmware version still older than recommended.
maria: quick mitigation: cordon + drain affected nodes to avoid provisioning into them, bump cluster autoscaler thresholds.
aj: what about eviction/cleaner settings? can we slow down scrub to reduce sustained IOPS?
infra-oncall: temporary mitigation: disabled aggressive ephemeral-cleaner cron on gpu-pool-3 and lowered scrub concurrency. Restarting kubelet on a test node now.
infra-bot: action: disabled job ephemeral-cleaner/gpu-pool-3 by infra-oncall
kevin: after disabling cleaner, I see writeback rates back to baseline and nodes start to recover. provisioning success rate rose from 55% -> 98% on test slice.
maria: follow-up: need firmware rollout plan and to add health gating to deploy that changes scrubbing settings. Also add KV cache on restart to reduce rehydrate IO.
aj: opened ticket for scrub config rollback + firmware: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3281
sre: recommend adding per-node IO caps for cleaner jobs: cgroups or ionice/nice wrapper.
infra-oncall: agree. next steps:
- roll back the aggressive scrub PR for gpu-pool-3
- schedule firmware updates with vendor (long lead)
- add pre-deploy lint to block changes that increase scrub concurrency without perf test
- instrument per-node scrub IOPS and inject alarms
kevin: logging note: please capture nvme SMART logs before we reboot nodes. run:
```
sudo smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1 > /tmp/nvme0-smart.log && kubectl cp /tmp/nvme0-smart.log $POD:/artifacts/
```
maria: thanks all. marking incident resolved for now, moving to postmortem.
aj: :thumbsup: 
infra-oncall: last check: provisioning stable across us-west2 gpu pools. Closing PD.
infra-bot: incident INC12345 closed by infra-oncall
